To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the density of glutamatergically‐defined boutons is highest dorsomedially, where inputs from the prefrontal cortex, amygdala, hippocampus and thalamus are most dense.

the density of VGlu1 and VGlu2 boutons in the striatum is higher in the matrix than in patches and that there is a gradient of VGlu1 boutons along the dorsoventral, mediolateral and rostrocaudal axes.

the densities of VGlu1 and VGlu2 boutons in the striatum are differentially organized, that this organization is in accordance with the known organization of cortical inputs to the striatal patch–matrix, and that the organization of VGlu1 boutons in the dorsal striatum coincides with the organization of cortical inputs from the prefrontal cortex to the dorsal striatum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organization of the striatum and how the organization is reflected in its synaptic input.
the organization of the striatum.
how the brain processes information, how it learns, how it controls behavior, and how it produces and perceives sensory information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the striatum is a highly complex and organized brain region with a high degree of heterogeneity.

the patch‐matrix organization in the rat dorsal striatum is not reflected by differences in density of VGlu1 or VGlu2 boutons, whereas the distribution of VGAT boutons is not as uniform as previously thought.
the density gradients of the VGluT1, VGluT 2, and VGAT immunoreactive boutons are not in accordance with the patch‐matrix topographic pattern of the striatal neuropil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the density of glutamatergics endings in the striatum is not random, but rather organized into a pattern that reflects the topography of the cortical and subcortically projecting inputs to the striatal patch-matrix.

the density of VGlu1 and VGlu2 boutons are different in patch and matrix compartments and that there is a gradient of VGlu1 boutons from ventral lateral to dorsal medial, whereas VGlu2 bouton density increases from lateral to medial.
the density of the glutamatergics endings are organized along three axes, and the density of the GABAergic endings are less organized.
The main takeaway from our work is that

glutamate‐ and γ‐aminobu- tyric acid (GAA)‐containing boutons show different density gradients in the striatum and these gradients are related to the known patch‐matrix organization of the striatum and the known cortical and subcorti- cal sources of these afferents.
the patch‐matrix organization of the striatum is reflected by the densities of glutamatergice endings.
the patch‐matrix topographic organization of the striatum is reflected in the densities of glutamatergics endings.
